subject: Renewal & upsell: proposal for increased capacity and temporary rate shelter
messages:
From: Alyssa Greene <alyssa.greene@epsilonhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@epsilonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + capacity increase: target Q2 start

Kimberly —

Hope you had a good weekend. We're coming up on our contract renewal with Redwood (end of April) and we have a near-term capacity need. Summary:
- Current monthly usage: ~6M tokens. Forecast for H2: +20% (we expect sustained +20–25% from targeted feature rollouts).
- Procurement timeline: need final commercial terms by 29 Mar to hit a 1 Apr invoicing cadence.

Primary asks:
1) Can Redwood provide pricing for a 12‑month renewal that incorporates a 20% committed capacity increase (convert from retainer to capacity commitment)?
2) Given some forecast risk from our product launch, would you consider a temporary "rate shelter" — hold current rates for the first 90 days post renewal and then migrate to the committed unit price?
3) Any short-term credits or overage protections you can offer to help with rollout spikes?

We'd like a single-page commercial summary we can circulate with procurement. Also please include estimated lead time for Dedicated capacity bump if needed.

Thanks — appreciate a quick outline today if possible.

Alyssa Greene
Head of Platform, Epsilon Health
alyssa.greene@epsilonhealth.com

Folks — forwarding Epsilon's ask. Quick context: Epsilon is a mid-sized health-tech customer, SOC2-compliant, on a retainer that they want to convert to committed capacity (+~20%). Procurement wants a commercial summary by 29 Mar.

Can we suggest a go-to-market construct that balances risk / margin:
- 12‑month committed capacity (20% uplift on current committed baseline)
- Temporary rate shelter (hold current unit rate for first 90 days) to ease onboarding spikes
- A limited credit mechanic for overages during the first 90 days (e.g., 30–50% credit applied to overage invoices)

Marissa — what's acceptable discount/credit threshold for a deal of this size?
David — any ops concerns on Dedicated capacity or burst pooling if they exceed forecast?

I'll draft a one-pager after we align. Attaching last year's renewal terms for reference.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
Attachment: prior_renewal_terms_2026.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + capacity increase: target Q2 start

Kimberly —

Thanks for the ping. My recommendation (commercial):
- Offer a 12‑month commit at an 8% discount off list committed unit price (applies to the committed capacity baseline).
- Temporary 90‑day rate shelter: keep their current effective rate for months 0–3. After month 3, the committed unit price (post-discount) applies.
- Overages during months 0–3: we apply a credit equal to 30% of overage charges (credited on the next invoice) to give them buffer for launch spikes. Eligibility requires a signed amendment that moves the baseline commit up by 20% (minimum).
- Require a 30‑day advance notice for Dedicated capacity activation; if they need immediate Dedicated pool spin-up we can offer a 10% surcharge for expedited provisioning and a max lead time of 7 business days.

Rationale: 8% keeps our ASP while giving them meaningful commercial comfort. The 30% overage credit is a temporary concession; operationally we should make clear it is a one-time intake credit for rollout.

David — confirm capacity lead time and any SLA caveats; if ops are tight we should instead route them to a hybrid burst model (shared burst pool + floor commit) to avoid long Dedicated procurement.

—Marissa
VP, Sales Strategy

Alyssa — thanks for the details and for the call last week. Attached is a one‑page commercial summary and an SOW redline that captures the solution we discussed. Summary below for quick circulation with procurement:

Commercial summary (proposal):
- Term: 12 months (rolling) starting on execution date.
- Commit: +20% on their existing committed capacity (baseline to be defined in amendment).
- Committed unit price: 8% discount off list committed unit price (applies after the 90‑day shelter).
- Temporary rate shelter: maintain current effective unit rate for the first 90 days post-execution.
- Overage protection (pilot period): for months 0–3, Redwood credits 30% of overage charges (credit applied to the invoice following the overage month).
- Dedicated capacity: 30 calendar day lead time for standard provisioning; expedited 7 business day option available with a 10% provisioning surcharge.

Operational notes:
- We recommend a hybrid approach for go‑live: committed capacity + shared burst pool. David will provide a short ops checklist and pre-provision headroom.
- Eligibility: amendments must be signed by 29 Mar to align with Epsilon's procurement cadence.

Next steps / asks for Epsilon procurement:
1) Confirm acceptance of the commercial summary by 29 Mar to secure the temporary rate shelter.
2) If you need Dedicated provisioning within 30 days of execution, confirm expedited provisioning so we reserve engineer allocation.
3) Sign and return the attached SOW redline; we'll issue a DocuSign package for execution (link included).

Attachments: Epsilon_Renewal_Proposal_20270322.pdf (one‑page commercial summary), Epsilon_SOW_redline_20270322.docx
